newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmiri separatist detained during protest march.
newsitem.headline: Kashmiri separatist detained during protest march.

text.p: Indian police detained a popular Kashmiri separatist leader on Saturday during a rally by about 200 people against alleged human rights violations by Indian troops, police said.
A police spokesman said they had detained separatist leader Shabir Ahmad Shah, who was leading the protest march in the heart of Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir state.
Police fired in the air and used tear gas to disperse the demonstrators.
"Indian forces stop innocent killing, rape and custodial killings," the protesters shouted. "We want freedom."
A group of leading Kashmiri separatists on Thursday said human rights violations by Indian security forces had increased rapidly in recent months. Authorities in Srinagar denied the allegations.

Dozens of guerrilla groups seeking a merger with neighbouring Pakistan or independence have been waging a rebellion in the Himalayan region since 1990. Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have died in insurgency-related violence since then.
